examples.question_text:
For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(Z<0.48)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline z&0.48\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.6844\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(Z>1.47)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline z&1.47\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.9292\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(0.45<Z<1.65)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.45&1.65\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.6736&0.9505\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(Z<-0.92)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline z&0.92\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.8212\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(Z>-1.43)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline z&1.43\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.9236\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(-1.72<Z<-0.56)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.56&1.72\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.7123&0.9573\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(-0.73<Z<1.46)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.73&1.46\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.7673&0.9279\\\hline\end{array}$

The masses of $1200$ packets are normally distributed with a mean of $250$ g and a standard deviation of $10$ g. Find the probability that a randomly chosen packet has a mass between $242$ g and $263$ g, then find the expected number of such packets. Round the count to the nearest whole packet.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.80&1.30\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.7881&0.9032\\\hline\end{array}$

Examination marks are normally distributed with a mean of $55$ and a standard deviation of $12$. Use the closest probability in the table to find the approximate mark separating the top $15\%$ from the remaining marks. Give your answer to one decimal place.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z&1.03&1.04&1.05\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.8485&0.8508&0.8531\\\hline\end{array}$

Completion times for a task are normally distributed with a mean of $80$ seconds and a standard deviation of $15$ seconds. Use the closest probability in the table to find the approximate time below which the fastest $25\%$ of times fall. Give your answer to one decimal place.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.66&0.67&0.68\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.7454&0.7486&0.7517\\\hline\end{array}$

coverage.summary: Repaired only example 9's diagnosed label collision: extended the −0.67 tick to y=-0.55 to stagger its label below the mean label, and moved the 70.0 s annotation to y=-1.2 to reserve a separate row. Font sizes, boundary association, palette, mathematics and wording are preserved. Examples 0–8 and all methods and mappings remain unchanged. The baseline has no existing examples, so existingExamples remains empty. Source-level gutter, diagram and annotation checks covered all ten candidate examples; these are not rendered acceptance. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither altered nor re-audited. No files were written, repository inspections run or subagents used. A scoped independent recheck and actual desktop/mobile rendered inspection remain required before publication.

examples.derivation: Direct cumulative lookup gives P(Z<0.48)=0.6844. The diagram shades the region left of 0.48.
P(Z>1.47)=1−0.9292=0.0708. The diagram shades the right tail above 1.47.
P(0.45<Z<1.65)=0.9505−0.6736=0.2769. The shaded interval matches both boundaries.
Symmetry gives P(Z<−0.92)=P(Z>0.92)=1−0.8212=0.1788. The negative left tail is shaded.
Symmetry gives P(Z>−1.43)=P(Z<1.43)=0.9236. The diagram shades everything above the negative boundary.
Reflecting the interval gives P(0.56<Z<1.72)=0.9573−0.7123=0.2450. The diagram retains the original negative interval.
P(Z<−0.73)=1−0.7673=0.2327; therefore P(−0.73<Z<1.46)=0.9279−0.2327=0.6952. The shading crosses the mean between the stated boundaries.

The boundaries standardise to (242−250)/10=−0.8 and (263−250)/10=1.3. The probability is 0.9032−(1−0.7881)=0.6913. Expected frequency is 1200×0.6913=829.56, rounding to 830 packets. Diagram boundaries and mass annotations agree.

The required cumulative probability is 0.85. Distances from the listed probabilities are 0.0015, 0.0008 and 0.0031, so z=1.04 is closest. The boundary is 55+1.04×12=67.48, rounding to 67.5 marks. The shaded upper tail is approximately 15%.

The lower-tail probability 0.25 corresponds by symmetry to a positive cumulative probability of 0.75. The distances from 0.75 are 0.0046, 0.0014 and 0.0017 for the supplied entries, so 0.7486 is closest and the required score is −0.67. The time is 80 + (−0.67) × 15 = 69.95 seconds, which rounds to 70.0 seconds. The diagram shades the correct left tail. Its dashed boundary has height 2 exp(−0.67²/2) ≈ 1.5978. Moving the boundary tick label below the mean label and reserving a further row for 70.0 s preserves their mathematical associations.

review.summary: All 31 exact assessment locators are mapped, and the ten examples cover every distinct assessed method. Example 9 follows the supplied reverse-lookup method combined with taught symmetry and stays within the accepted assessment scope. The scoped repair passes source, mathematical and diagram-code review. Retained examples were checked for gutters and diagram annotations without repeating their accepted mathematics. Automatic solution colouring preserves editable prose. Actual desktop/mobile capture must still confirm label separation and final typography before publication; rendered acceptance is not claimed.
